thread:
lina (support): heads up — Seatly just escalated. They say a prompt that's been stable for months started returning unrelated instructions after last night's rollout in eu-west-1. Ticket #SE-1892.

aj (seatly-customer): hey team — we saw this around 03:12 UTC. Same prompt, same model id we've been using, but responses changed to procedural steps that are incorrect for our domain. Not seeing it in us-west.

lina (support): can you paste the exact request you sent and the response you expect vs what you got?

aj (seatly-customer): sure. minimal repro:

```json
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "redwood-large-v2",
  "model_version": "2026-03-07-canary",
  "input": "Summarize the following transaction ledger entry for display: \"PAYMENT to ACME CO - INV 4433 - 2026-03-10 - $1,240.00\""
}
```

Expected: a one-line friendly summary like "Payment to Acme Co for invoice 4433, $1,240.00"
Got: a multi-step instruction list telling the user how to process refunds and run a reconciliation script. (completely wrong intent)

lina (support): thanks. did you repro this across multiple requests or just that one?

aj (seatly-customer): reproducible ~60% of the time from eu-west-1 on A100 nodes. We tried pinning older version (2026-02-28) and it looks fine. Also tried eu-central-1 which is H100 and it's fine there.

carl (eng-runtime): pinging in. @lina can you attach the request_id and the response payload we received? Also which cluster names?

lina (support): attaching logs — request_id=rx-7f9a3b, cluster=eu-west-1-a100-pool-3. Full response included in support ticket. Noting that client used model_version field set to 2026-03-07-canary.

sara (mlops): this smells like a kernel/quantization mismatch on A100 path. We rolled the new tokenizer + int8 kernel selector to canary in eu regions last night at 02:40 UTC. Deploy-bot reported success:

deploy-bot: canary deployment 2026-03-07-canary -> redwood-large-v2 to eu-* completed at 2026-03-07T02:41:12Z :white_check_mark:

carl (eng-runtime): good — that matches timing. @sara can you check model variant routing? Is canary correctly routing to quantized int8 kernels only on certain instance types? We need to know why semantics drifted.

sara (mlops): checking. Preliminary: kernel-selector picked int8 kernels for A100 and fp16 for H100. We have heuristics that prefer int8 on A100 to save tokens/costs. Might be a conversion bug in tokenization mapping for some byte pair sequences that only trigger on EU tokenizer locale or an updated vocab.

dennis (eng-sre): I'm seeing increased content-regression alerts for eu-west-1 between 02:45-03:30 UTC. Error rates for model-quality checks jumped from 0.3% -> 4.8% (heuristic: intent-preservation check on control prompt set). Latency slightly lower on A100 (expected) but quality alerts up.

carl (eng-runtime): urgent repro steps we need from eng side: 1) exact request/response pair (we have it), 2) stack trace or kernel selection logs for that request, 3) whether KV cache or prefix-cache changed. @ops-bot can you pull the kernel selection trace for request_id rx-7f9a3b?

ops-bot: fetching traces for rx-7f9a3b... attached: kernel_selector.log, qconfig.json, runtime-metrics.csv

lina (support): uploaded logs to ticket. Noting extra info: the customer reported this also happens when setting "precision": "int8" explicitly.

sara (mlops): looking at kernel_selector.log — for rx-7f9a3b we selected int8_path_v2 with vocab_remap=enabled. There's a remapping table change in 2026-03-07 canary: 

```diff
- remap_table_v1.json
+ remap_table_v2.json  // added 4 entries for euro currency variants
```

That remap can alter tokenization on sequences containing currency symbols and invoice-like patterns. If remap mapping is wrong it could change token boundaries and produce different completions.

carl (eng-runtime): that would explain domain-shift for ledger-like prompts. @sara can you roll back remap_table for canary in eu and re-run a small AB test against Seatly's exact input?

sara (mlops): yes. Rolling remap_table -> remap_table_v1 on eu-a100 canary nodes now.

deploy-bot: rolling remap_table rollback to eu-west-1-a100-pool-3 started at 2026-03-07T04:12:08Z

ops-bot: change applied to nodes: eu-west-1-a100-pool-3 (3/3)

aj (seatly-customer): retesting now...

aj (seatly-customer): update: behavior back to expected for the same request. Thanks. Seems fixed for our test. We still see occasional flakiness but much reduced.

lina (support): marking ticket as escalated->engineering, but customer is satisfied with rollback result. Need postmortem and follow-up plan.

carl (eng-runtime): next steps: 1) create a short postmortem that includes root cause: remap_table_v2 introduced tokenization boundary changes for euro/invoice patterns causing intent drift on int8 path on A100; 2) Add automated unit tests for invoice/transaction prompts in CI for any remap_table changes; 3) Add a preflight check that runs canary on a small regional control set including EU A100 pods; 4) revert canary until we have safe remap.

sara (mlops): will open PR to add control set and add a checklist item to the canary playbook. Also we'll add a metric that alerts when intent-preservation falls >1% on control set per-region.

dennis (eng-sre): also recommending a quick monitoring tweak: surface model-variant-level quality deltas in the Console so customers see regional diffs. Filed an infra ticket.

carl (eng-runtime): thanks everyone. Lina, please add notes to the customer ticket and let Seatly know we'll run a longer soak test before reintroducing remap_table_v2.

lina (support): will do. adding 'postmortem_expected' tag and booking a brief sync with Seatly for Friday. :thumbsup:

aj (seatly-customer): appreciate the quick response team. keep us posted.

-- end of thread --
